introduce KV freelist defragmenter and selective hot-prefix pinning


Motivation: under high-concurrency, the paged KV cache freelist would fragment after repeated allocations/frees of mixed-size blocks, increasing allocation latency and causing more frequent slow-path compaction. This PR adds an opportunistic freelist defragmenter that compacts adjacent free pages on free-paths and a lightweight hot-prefix selective pinning policy so frequently-accessed key prefixes avoid costly eviction. Goals: reduce p99 allocation latency, lower background compaction pressure, and improve tail latency for workloads with hot prefixes (chat sessions, long contexts).

Summary of changes:
- Opportunistic freelist defragmenter run inline on frees when a small threshold of contiguous free segments is observed (configurable).
- Compact-on-free path that coalesces adjacent free pages into larger blocks to improve reuse for larger token sequences.
- Adaptive reuse scoring: tracks short-term reuse frequency per page bucket and prefers reuse of high-score pages.
- Hot-prefix selective pinning: a small resident pin set for top-N hot key prefixes with LRU eviction; pins are persisted across ephemeral reconnects to stabilize performance.

Motivation: Improve streaming resilience for mobile/unreliable clients and make client-initiated cancel behavior idempotent while preserving OpenAI compatibility. This PR introduces a 'streaming session snapshot' model and explicit client ACK semantics so disconnected clients can reconnect and resume without inconsistent tool calls or duplicate function invocations. Includes small API surface additions (resume_token, session_id, seq) exposed in the OpenAI-compatible streaming adapter.

claims.text: A 'streaming session snapshot' model and explicit client ACK semantics were introduced to allow disconnected clients to reconnect from a safe checkpoint using a server issued marker plus an explicit receipt from the client, while keeping compatibility with existing OpenAI like streaming clients.

citations.text: Summary: Introduces a configurable tool result merge policy and a per-invocation exponential backoff/retry budget aimed at improving ergonomics and determinism for parallel/multi-tool calls. Motivation: the previous default (inject-first-returned) caused nondeterministic structured-output injection when multiple tools returned overlapping JSON fragments or produced idempotent but out-of-order updates. This led to subtle regressions in downstream parsers and customer incidents (SUP-9021). Design: add three merge strategies: first_wins (legacy), last_wins, and merge_patch (depth-aware JSON/struct merge that preserves keyed identities and deduplicates array items when an id key is present). Implement a per-call RetryPolicy that exposes base_delay_ms, factor, max_attempts, max_delay_ms, jitter_pct and an overall retry_budget_ms to avoid retry storms that starve streaming tokens. Improves TP allreduce performance on clusters with heterogeneous link bandwidth by introducing a bandwidth-aware fanout planner and KV-shard coalescing. Adds a small stride-optimized memcpy kernel and stream mapping to reduce comm/computation stalls. Opt-in flag and canary plan included.

What changed (high level):
- Fanout planner: builds a minimal spanning fanout for allreduce that avoids slow links and increases per-hop concurrency when it detects bandwidth heterogeneity. The planner prefers intra-node NVLink-RDMA pairs, then high-rate cross-node links, and uses low-rate links only as fallback.
- KV-shard coalescer: groups adjacent KV cache shards into aligned coalesced writes to reduce the number of small allgathers. This reduces per-step launch overhead and amortizes DMA for common prefix cache hits.
- Stride-optimized memcpy kernel: a small, vectorized kernel for <4KB strided copies used by the coalescer; reduces memcpy time by up to 3x in microbenchmarks.

Compatibility and safety:
- The fanout planner is opt-in via config flag "runtime.bandwidth_fanout.enabled" (default: true for Dedicated and Private, false for Hosted until canary completes).
- Fallbacks: if topology probe fails or detects homogeneous links, planner falls back to existing balanced tree.
- Unit and integration tests added; new runtime flag is gated behind a feature flag at rollout.

- [x] Docs: added runtime flags and rollout notes
